title: Minimum Weight to Reach Value Threshold
statement:
You are given `n` items. Item `i` has a weight `w[i]` and a value `v[i]`. You are also given a target value `T`.

This is the inverse of the classic knapsack problem: instead of maximizing value under a weight limit, you must choose a subset of items (each item can be chosen **at most once**) whose total value is **at least** `T`, and among all such subsets minimize the total weight.

Print the minimum possible total weight. If even taking all items does not reach a total value of `T`, print `-1`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `T`.
The second line contains `n` integers `w[0] ... w[n-1]`, the weights.
The third line contains `n` integers `v[0] ... v[n-1]`, the values.
outputFormat: Print the minimum total weight of a subset with total value at least `T`, or `-1` if no such subset exists.

examples.explanation: No single item reaches value 7, and the pairs {0,1} and {1,2} only reach 5 and 6. The pairs {0,2} (value 7, weight 9) and {1,3} (value 7, weight 9) reach it, and {0,3} does too but weighs 10. The minimum weight is 9.
All three items together have value 9 < 10, so the target cannot be reached.

hints: The weights are large, so a table indexed by weight is too big. The target value is small, so index the table by value instead.
Let dp[j] be the minimum weight needed to reach total value at least j (cap values at T). dp[0] = 0 and everything else starts as infinity.
Process items one by one, and update j downward so each item is used at most once: dp[min(T, j + v)] = min(dp[min(T, j + v)], dp[j] + w).
